why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim: channels-reference.md line 225 is exactly 'Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params:' — a one-sentence line, followed by a table whose rows are `content` (string, 'The event body') and `meta` (Record<string,string>, optional, becomes attributes on the <channel> tag). Line 48 ('Emit `notifications/claude/channel` events when something happens') and line 221 ('call `mcp.notification()` with method `notifications/claude/channel`') say the same thing; the page uses the un-prefixed string `claude/channel` only as the CAPABILITY key (`capabilities.experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} }`, line ~101). The page is a legitimate Claude contract source: it is row 67 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv. (2) The cited code says what was claimed: packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114 is `const ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema = NotificationSchema.extend({ method: z.literal('claude/channel') })` and :357-361 is `setNotificationHandler(ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema, notification => { const text = (notification.params as { text?: unknown } | undefined)?.text; ... })`. `grep -ran 'notifications/claude' packages apps scripts` (with -a, NUL-safe) returns 0 hits; the only repo hits are the sweep documents themselves in docs/. Every other notification this same client registers carries the prefix (ToolListChangedNotificationSchema = 'notifications/tools/list_changed'), which is what makes the un-prefixed literal a rename-class miss rather than a style choice. (3) The CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier, both one layer up and one layer down. Down: MCP SDK dispatch keys on the exact method string — protocol.js:274 `this._notificationHandlers.get(notification.method) ?? this.fallbackNotificationHandler`, with `if (handler === undefined) return;` under the comment 'Ignore notifications not being subscribed to'; setNotificationHandler registers under `getMethodLiteral(schema)`. No `fallbackNotificationHandler` is set anywhere in packages/ or apps/, and the custom SupervisedStdioClientTransport (client.ts:820-840) deserializes and forwards frames unmodified — there is no compat shim rewriting the method. So a conforming server's notification is dropped with no error, exactly as claimed. Up: the consumer chain is McpChannelMessage { server, text } -> NessyMcpClient.channelHandler -> McpClientPool.dispatchChannelMessage (mcp-pool.ts:1082) guarded by isMcpChannelMessage (:370, requires `message.text` to be a string) -> SessionManager channel listener; nothing anywhere reads `content` or `meta`, so even a server that used the un-prefixed method would still be ignored unless it sent `text`. Not an owner decision: inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions contain no channel-method row (its only channel item is `isManagedChannelServerAllowed`, a different symbol in the managed-policy subsystem, listed in section 4 as a consequence-false false positive). Not a deliberate product difference either — this is a wire method on the MCP protocol, not a NESSY_ rebrand surface, and the code already names it `claude/channel`; the feature is explicitly modeled on Claude channels (storage.ts:1142 'Whether a connected MCP server may push text into a live turn through the `claude/channel` notification'). The parity audit already grades this area 'partial' rather than parity (2026-07-25 audit line 1764). Two bounding caveats that do not refute it: channel push is fail-closed (`mcpChannelPushEnabled` defaults false, CHANNEL_PUSH_OFF), so no user is affected until they opt in; and the claim's own line 'grep returns zero hits repo-wide' is now true only for source — docs/ quotes the string.
correctedState: Confirmed. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114 registers the channel notification under the literal method `claude/channel`, which is Claude's CAPABILITY key (`capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`), not its notification method — the documented method is `notifications/claude/channel` (channels-reference.md:225, also :48 and :221). The handler at :357-361 then reads `params.text`, while the documented params are `content` (string) and optional `meta` (Record<string,string>). Because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dispatches notifications by exact method string (protocol.js:273-277) and this client sets no fallbackNotificationHandler and does not rewrite frames in SupervisedStdioClientTransport, a channel server written to Claude's contract has every event silently discarded. `meta` is unsupported at the type level too: McpChannelMessage (client.ts:102-105) carries only { server, text }, and isMcpChannelMessage (mcp-pool.ts:370) requires `text`. Exposure is bounded — mcpChannelPushEnabled defaults to false, so no dispatcher is installed until a user opts in — but the mismatch means the feature cannot work with any conforming channel plugin. Fix is to accept `notifications/claude/channel` with `content`/`meta` (keeping `claude/channel`/`text` as a read-path alias if any in-house server already emits it), and to plumb `meta` through to the <channel> tag attributes, which is the separate phase1 row 22.
